text:
Alisa: Heads-up — we just saw a spike of GPU pod evictions in ap-southeast1 around 06:12 UTC. ~120 evictions over 15m, latency up on a few realtime queues. Cost also spiking because jobs are resubmitting to higher-flavor nodes.
Sam: Seen it too. KC metric shows NVLink retransmits + conntrack churn on the warm pool nodes. Packets got queued and some attach operations timed out -> kubelet dropped pods then scheduler rescheduled to different racks.
Priya: Do we know which workloads are the hot ones? tiny-gang jobs again?
Alisa: Mostly small-batch training and a few RL evals that request fractional GPUs and use gang scheduling. They tend to land with mixed affinity which fragments racks.
Mike: Can repro locally on a test rack: when tiny-gang spread hits a compact rack + NVLink saturation, attach latency > 3s and attach-detach retries bubble. That triggers preemption in our scheduler under 5s grace because preemption window is small.
Sam: Suggest immediate mitigation: increase attach timeout/retry and bump scheduler preempt window to 30s for ap-southeast1 (reduce noisy preempts). Also temporarily mark one warm pool node pool as "isolation-prefer" to absorb tiny-gangs.
Priya: Agree. Also we should throttle fractional-gang churn: add a quota for tiny-gang concurrency in that region for 24h while we stabilize.
Alisa: I can roll a small patch to autoscaler and scheduler flags. Proposed change:
```yaml
# scheduler flag tweak (kube-scheduler-config snippet)
preemption:
  minPreemptionTimeSeconds: 30
  maxPreemptionCandidates: 10
# autoscaler: limit tiny-gang concurrent launches
scaleConfig:
  gangJobs:
    tiny-gang-concurrency-limit: 60
```
Sam: Nice. For the warm-pool isolation, ops-bot can label one node pool and set a nodeAffinity for tiny-gang workloads? We should avoid broad taints that break other customers.
Mike: Ops steps: 1) label pool: `kubectl label nodepool ap-southeast1-warmnode pool=isol-prefer` 2) patch Tiny gang job controller to prefer nodeSelector `pool=isol-prefer` (soft prefer). That reduces cross-rack attach churn.
Alisa: I'll do the scheduler autoscaler patch in staging now and flip to canary. Priya can you submit the concurrency quota change?
Priya: On it. I'll open a short-lived quota CR and post the link.
ops-bot: Deploy started: scheduler-config patch -> canary in ap-southeast1 (deployment id: d-17577-canary). Logs pushed to #eng-platform-deploys.
Sam: After canary we should monitor: evictions, attach latency, NVLink errors, and cost per token. If evictions drop and cost stabilizes we'll expand region-wide.
Mike: Also add a short telemetry alert: if attach latency > 2s for > 5m, mute noisy autoscaler decisions and surface as page.
Alisa: Will follow up with a mini postmortem in the channel tomorrow with numbers. For now rolling the canary. :thumbsup:
Priya: Thanks — will coordinate the quota PR and add a note to runbook (how to isolate warm pool).
Sam: Good plan. One follow-up: let's catalog which jobs tolerate requeueing vs which are sensitive so we can set evictionPriority. That will make long-term binpacking cleaner.
Alisa: Agree, adding to backlog: job-sensitivity matrix + a scheduler policy experiment (soft-affinity + longer preempt window).
